disclaimer: Facts are reported as stated by the named sources, with links. This is information, not advice, and not a rating of any company.

topics.title: Most people don't want one nearby
topics.stat_label: oppose a data center in their area, in three national polls this year
topics.summary: Three national polls in 2026 found 65% to 75% of people oppose an AI data center near them. One pollster that repeats the same question saw opposition climb from 42% in August 2025 to 75% in August 2026. Voters get a direct say soon: 38 local ballot measures in eight states, 34 of them on the November 3 ballot.
topics.note: The polls ask different questions. One offered a 'neither' option, which lowers the share who oppose.

topics.title: Governments are adding rules
topics.stat_label: formal public actions in 25 states, per one tracker
topics.summary: States and towns are acting. Texas has gone furthest, as reported: a pause on new grid connections, penalties for not reporting water use, and a hold on environmental permits. Across the country, 32 states have approved special electricity rates for very large users. These usually mean 10 to 20 year contracts and a minimum monthly bill.
topics.note: The Texas orders are known from press reports; the orders themselves have not been pulled yet.

topics.title: Building is still booming
topics.summary: Existing space is nearly full, and 80% of what is under construction is already leased. A record 7.5 GW is being built, with Atlanta now the biggest construction market. Announced large projects add up to more than 71 GW and $1.13 trillion.

topics.title: But many projects stall
topics.stat_label: local groups in 40 states opposing projects
topics.summary: Trackers count dozens of projects blocked or delayed by local opposition, 75 of them (about $130 billion) in the first quarter of 2026 alone by one count. One analyst firm argues most of those were early-stage plans without land, money or a grid connection, and says its forecast for 2026 building barely moved.
topics.note: Counts use different periods and definitions, so they don't add up to one number.

topics.title: The bottlenecks: equipment, workers, approval
topics.stat_label: wait for a large power transformer
topics.summary: Large transformers take about two and a half years to arrive, with a 30% supply shortfall. Construction is short roughly 439,000 workers, and data center jobs pay up to 30% more. CBRE says getting local approval now matters as much as getting power.

claims.statement: The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott announced on 2026-08-03 a moratorium on new data centers connecting to the state grid, and ordered ERCOT to require developers to provide information on tax breaks, power use, water, community impact and ownership.
The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott directed the Texas Water Development Board on 2026-09-15 to penalize data centers that fail to report water use; only 28% had answered a mandatory survey.

The Texas Tribune reports Gov. Abbott ordered the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality on 2026-09-21 to stop issuing environmental permits for data centers until audits are complete. No end date was given.
Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 75 projects worth about $130 billion blocked or delayed in Q1 2026.
Data Center Watch (10a Labs), as relayed by Gizmodo, counted 45 projects worth about $68 billion blocked or delayed from April to June 2026.

SemiAnalysis argues most projects flagged as 'canceled' are early-stage ones without site control, financing or interconnection. It says its 2026 North America hyperscaler self-build forecast moved only about 1%, and colocation under 5%, over six months.
The dcmap.us tracker lists 56 formal public actions across 25 states (22 statewide, 34 local), with entries through August 2026.
claims.source_name: dcmap.us: US Data Center Policy Tracker

claims.statement: Gallup, in a poll fielded 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-18 (1,000 adults, margin of error about 4 points), found 71% oppose construction of AI data centers in their local area and 27% favor. 48% strongly oppose.
claims.source_name: Gallup: Americans Oppose AI Data Centers in Their Area

claims.statement: The UMass Amherst Poll, fielded 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-26 (1,000 respondents, margin of error 3.5 points), found 65% oppose, 11% support and 24% neither, when asked about an AI data center in their local community.

Embold Research, for Heatmap, fielded 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-13 (2,045 registered voters, margin of error 2.3 points) and found 75% would oppose a data center built near their home, 61% strongly (per Heatmap News).
Heatmap's four polls show opposition rising from 42% (Aug 2025, with 43% in support) to 51% (Feb 2026), 70% (May 2026) and 75% (Aug 2026), per Heatmap News.

Ballotpedia counts 38 data-center-related ballot measures in eight states in 2026, including 20 in Ohio across 17 jurisdictions. 34 of the 38 are on the 2026-11-03 ballot. In the four earlier 2026 votes, voters favored greater restrictions each time.
claims.source_name: Ballotpedia News: data center ballot measures

claims.statement: EEI's list, dated 2026-09-11, catalogs publicly announced large-load projects of about 20 MW or more, totaling more than $1.13 trillion of investment and more than 71 GW of connected load. It says 32 states have approved large-load tariffs and 7 more are pending.
claims.source_name: EEI: Large Load Projects and Tariffs (Sept 2026)

claims.statement: CoBank, describing the SEPA and NCCETC DELTa database, says a common large-load rate design has emerged: contracts of 10 to 20 years, minimum bills of about 70 to 100% of contracted capacity, and collateral and exit rules.
claims.source_name: SEPA and NCCETC: DELTa large-load tariff database

claims.statement: CBRE says U.S. data center vacancy hit a record low of 1.4% in H1 2026 (0.2% in Northern Virginia), and that 80.4% of under-construction capacity is already preleased.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: CBRE says under-construction capacity rose 24.8% to a record 7,481.1 MW, with Atlanta (2,882 MW) overtaking Northern Virginia as the top construction market.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: CBRE writes that "the ability to secure local approval has become as critical to site selection as power and fiber availability," and that power availability and infrastructure delivery timelines remain the most decisive siting factors.
claims.source_name: CBRE: North America Data Center Trends H1 2026

claims.statement: Urban Land, citing Bloomberg, reports local opposition has stalled or blocked at least 48 U.S. data center projects (about $156 billion), that cancellations rose from 6 in 2024 to 25 in 2025, and that about 188 local groups operate in 40 states.
claims.source_name: Urban Land Institute: The Rising Cost of Data Center Pushback

claims.statement: POWER magazine, citing a Wood Mackenzie Q2 2025 survey, reports lead times of 128 weeks for power transformers, 144 weeks for generator step-up units, and 44 weeks for switchgear.

POWER magazine, citing Wood Mackenzie, reports a 30% supply deficit for power transformers and 10% for distribution transformers in 2025, with power transformer demand up 119% and prices up 77% since 2019, and data centers named as a major driver.

ITIF, citing a Wall Street Journal article of 2025-11-29, says the construction industry faced a 439,000-worker shortage driven by data center growth, and that data center construction roles pay up to 30% more than typical construction jobs.
